content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

The baseline specification is ready for review:

- [Specification](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/spec.md)
- [Quality checklist](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/checklists/requirements.md)
- Feature directory: `specs/001-manage-bookmarks`
- Validation: all checklist items passed; no unresolved clarifications

The draft assumes a personal, single-user web app with saving, editing, search, tags, favorites, archiving, and deletion. Accounts, sharing, sync, browser extensions, and import/export are excluded from the first release.

Please approve the specification or describe any changes. Once approved, I’ll prepare the implementation plan; no code has been written yet.

Thanks for putting this together — it reads clearly and a lot of it matches what I pictured. But a few things I really expected are either missing or ruled out, and I'd want them sorted before we call this the baseline.

- **The app filling in the details for me.** When I paste a link, I don't want to type the title myself every time. I expect the app to go look at the page and pull in its title, a short description, the little site icon, and ideally a preview image — and then I can tweak those if I want. I noticed you've put "automatic metadata retrieval" as out of scope. That's actually one of the main reasons I want this instead of just a browser's bookmarks, so I'd like it back in.

- **"Read it later."** I want to be able to mark a link as something I still need to read, see just those unread ones on their own, and then mark one as read so it drops off that list. I don't see that anywhere. I do see "favorites" — that's fine to have, but it's not the same thing as the read-later list I'm describing, so I'd want the read-later behavior too.

- **Doing things to several at once.** When I'm tidying up, I'd like to select a bunch of bookmarks and, say, add a tag to all of them, or archive or delete them together — including "apply to everything currently showing" when I've filtered the list. Right now everything seems to be one-at-a-time.

- **Smarter searching.** Plain text search is good, but I'd also want to search by a tag specifically (something like typing the tag with a marker in front of it), and to combine terms — this tag and that word, or one tag or another. And when I start typing a tag on a bookmark, it should suggest tags I've already used so I don't make duplicates.

- **Saving a search I use a lot.** If I set up a search plus some tags I care about, I'd like to save that combination and come back to it later without rebuilding it.

- **Keeping a copy of the page.** I'd like the app to hold onto a snapshot of what the page looked like when I saved it, so if it changes or disappears later I can still see it.

- **A couple of smaller things:** being able to sort the list different ways (not just newest first), and a place to adjust basic display preferences.

I'm not asking for accounts, sharing, sync, or browser extensions — those can stay out. But the pieces above are core to how I'd actually use this. Could you fold them in and show me the updated version?

The specification has been updated and revalidated:

- [Updated specification](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/spec.md)
- [Quality checklist](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/checklists/requirements.md)

It now treats all requested capabilities as core scope:

- Automatic title, description, site icon, and preview-image retrieval
- Editable metadata with explicit refresh behavior
- Dated page snapshots with retry, refresh, and failure states
- Read-later/unread tracking
- Combined text and `#tag` searches with AND/OR behavior
- Reusable tag suggestions
- Saved searches containing query, filters, and sorting
- Individual selection and “all current results” bulk actions
- Multiple sorting options
- Theme and information-density preferences

I made two bounded defaults explicit: new bookmarks are considered read unless marked for later, and one current snapshot is retained per bookmark rather than snapshot history.

All quality checks pass and no clarification markers remain. Please approve this revised baseline or identify further changes. Once approved, I’ll move to the planning gate.

This is much closer to what I had in mind — the page-details, snapshot, read-later, saved searches, bulk actions, sorting, and display bits all read right. The two defaults you called out are fine by me: I'm happy for a new link to count as already read unless I say "read later," and keeping just the one latest snapshot rather than a whole history is sensible.

One area I want to push on a little more before we lock this in: **searching**. You've got "this and that" and "this or that," which is great, but I'd also expect two more everyday things:

- **Leaving something out** — like "show me everything about cooking but *not* the ones tagged recipes." Being able to exclude a word or a tag.
- **An exact phrase** — if I put a few words in quotes, I want just that exact wording, not each word scattered around.

And when I combine several of these, I'd want a way to group them so the app doesn't guess wrong about what goes with what — say, this word, and then either of two tags, treated as a set.

Everything else in this version matches how I'd actually use the app. Fold in those search pieces and I think the baseline's there.

content:
The baseline specification now includes the remaining search behavior:

- `NOT` exclusions for words, phrases, tags, and grouped expressions
- Double-quoted exact phrases
- Parentheses for grouping
- Defined precedence: parentheses → NOT → AND → OR
- Clear handling for unmatched quotes, parentheses, and incomplete operators
- Saved searches retain the complete expression

Example: `cooking NOT #recipes (#vegan OR #quick)`.

The [updated specification](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/spec.md) passes the [quality checklist](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/checklists/requirements.md) with no unresolved clarifications.

If you approve this as the baseline, I’ll move to the implementation-planning gate next.

That's exactly what I was after — being able to leave things out, quote an exact phrase, and group things so the app doesn't misread what I meant. The cooking example reads just how I'd think about it.

This version of the spec matches how I actually want to use the app, across the board — saving with the details filled in and a snapshot kept, my read-later list, the searching, saved searches, working on many at once, sorting, and the display options. I'm happy with this as the baseline. Go ahead and move on to planning the build.

content:
The implementation plan is ready for approval. No application code or task breakdown has been created yet.

Key decisions:

- TypeScript on Node.js 24 LTS
- React/Vite client with a Fastify server
- SQLite for structured data; local files for snapshots and images
- Asynchronous, restart-safe metadata and snapshot processing
- Full-page WebP snapshots
- A bounded parser and parameterized query compiler for the search language
- Explicit protection against private-network URL fetching and unsafe archived content
- Unit, contract, integration, security, and browser-level testing

Node 24’s LTS status, Fastify’s schema-validation model, Playwright’s full-page capture support, and SQLite’s capacity informed these choices: [Node releases](https://nodejs.org/en/about/previous-releases), [Fastify validation](https://fastify.dev/docs/latest/Reference/Validation-and-Serialization/), [Playwright screenshots](https://playwright.dev/docs/screenshots), [SQLite limits](https://sqlite.org/limits.html).

- [Implementation plan](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/plan.md)

It contains 75 sequentially numbered tasks:

- Setup: 7
- Shared foundation and security: 10
- Enriched bookmarks and snapshots: 16
- Read-later: 6

- Bulk organization: 9
- Display preferences: 5
- Final hardening and validation: 8

There are 37 identified parallel opportunities. Every task follows the required checklist format and includes concrete file paths.

The suggested first usable milestone is saving a URL, automatically enriching it, safely retaining a snapshot, editing its details, and reopening either the live page or snapshot. Each later feature has its own independent test checkpoint.

No application code has been written yet. The project is now ready for the implementation gate.

That breakdown looks sensible to me, and the grouping lines up with everything we agreed on — the enriched saving and snapshots, read-later, the search and saved views, working on many at once, sorting, and display settings are all there. content:
A runnable integrated build is now available at:

**http://maker:4000/**

Implemented in this checkpoint:

- URL-only bookmark saving with asynchronous metadata retrieval
- Safe full-page snapshots and snapshot viewer
- Editing, tags, favorites, read-later, archive, restore, and deletion
- Search grammar with phrases, tags, NOT, AND, OR, and parentheses
- Saved searches
- Explicit and all-results bulk actions with count confirmation
- Sorting and display settings
- Responsive light/dark/system interface
- Private-network fetch blocking and inert snapshot delivery
- Persistent SQLite storage

Validation completed:

- Type checking passed
- Production build passed
- 20 automated tests passed
- End-to-end browser test passed
- Live metadata and snapshot capture succeeded
- Production dependency audit reports zero known vulnerabilities
- Health and readiness endpoints passed

The detailed evidence is in [validation/final.md](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/validation/final.md). The full 75-task checklist remains intentionally current in [tasks.md](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/tasks.md); unchecked items represent deeper exhaustive testing and hardening still outstanding rather than work being falsely claimed complete.

I've had a proper poke around and it does what I hoped. I saved a link with just its address and it went and filled in the title and kept a snapshot on its own. I tried adding the very same link again and instead of making a duplicate it told me it's already saved and pointed me at the existing one — exactly the behavior I wanted. My read-later list shows the right item, and the searching holds up: I tried leaving a tag out, an exact phrase in quotes, and combining things, and each gave me what I'd expect. The snapshot opens as a saved copy separate from the live page.

It looks calm and tidy too, and I like that it keeps everything right here on my device. This matches what we agreed the app should do, across saving and enriching, read-later, the searching and saved views, tidying up in bulk, sorting, and the display options.

I understand there's still some deeper testing and polishing on your list, and I'm fine with that continuing — it doesn't change that the app does what I asked for. I'm happy to accept it as it stands. Thank you for building this.
